lesson.title: 7.2 Why is she cold? Because it's windy
lesson.unit_title: Everyday needs, plans and free time
lesson.unit_outcome: Say what hurts and why someone feels a certain way, describe what people are wearing and the weather as it happens, tell someone to put on or take off clothes, talk about what people like doing, invite and answer, ask someone to repeat or explain, talk about being sick, the months and seasons, compare with the biggest and the tallest, and say what people and animals can do and are good at.
lesson.lesson_title: Why is she cold? Because it's windy
lesson.sub_lesson_title: Why is she cold? Because it's windy
lesson.goal: Ask why someone feels a certain way with Why …? and answer with Because … (Why is she cold? Because it's windy.).
lesson.grammar_function: A follow-up of A1 7.2 How Are You?: A1 asks how someone is and answers with a feeling (How is she? She is sad.); A1+ 7.2 asks why. The one new grammar relationship is Why + be + person + feeling? answered with Because + a reason (Why is she cold? Because it's windy.), then joined into one sentence (She's cold because it's windy.). The reasons are things A1 and A1+ already taught: the weather (A1 7.4), being sick (A1 7.9), running (A1 Unit 1) and 7.1's hurts. Two new feelings join A1 7.2's: worried and excited, each with a reason the photo shows (Diego is worried because his dog is sick. / Ana is excited because it's her birthday.).
lesson.prerequisite: A1 7.2 How are you? feelings; A1 7.4 weather; A1 7.9 sick; A1+ 3.3 he's/she's + -ing; A1+ 7.1 hurts.
lesson.speaking_outcome: Say Why with a rising start and a falling end (WHY is she COLD?); say because as bi-KOZ with the stress on the second part. Do not require native-like speed.

models.text: Why is she cold? Because it's windy.
Why is Diego worried? Because his dog is sick.
Why is Ana excited? Because it's her birthday.
Why are you thirsty? Because I'm running.
